top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) rests on a distinct idea, magic-wavelength trapping, that created a new large-ensemble regime and has been reproduced and compared between independent laboratories at the 1e-18 level, where the results confront atomic many-body theory. The two-name credit is compact and the lineage objection (2005 comb, 2012 single quantum systems) is answerable. P002 (twisted bilayer graphene) is a striking prediction-then-discovery case that I defer to condensed-matter colleagues on, but at eight years with an unresolved pairing mechanism and a contested credit (Yuan Cao, earlier moire theory) it is less mature, so I rank it second ahead of no award.
recusal_note: No collaboration with Katori or Ye. My close collaborators (L'Huillier, Keller's group, Dahlstrom, Argenti, Schuch, Indelicato) are not credited in any proposal. I work in precision atomic theory, the broad field of P001, and have supplied theory to experiments near the clock community; disclosed, not disqualifying.
